channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Building a Reliable Gaming Setup Advisor: Rules, Data, and Honest Recommendations
item.description: A look at how to design a trustworthy gaming setup advisor: separate hardware specs from real in-game performance, be clear about what can and cannot be verified, and structure the recommendations honestly, with a PS5 advisor as the worked example.

item.title: Stop Nesting Your Dash and Dive Events in GDevelop — Here's Why They Get Stuck
item.description: A hands-on GDevelop debugging guide explaining why nested dash and dive events fuse into an unmovable blob, and how 2D platformer developers can avoid this common trap.

item.title: Dead Keys: I Brought Back the Typing Games. Kiro Did the Heavy Lifting.
item.description: The author rebuilt 1980s arcade typing games with Kiro, turning missed keys into lessons, and documented the Kiroween 2026 hackathon build.

item.title: GDevelop vs Godot: The "Toy Engine" Myth Is Costing You Time
item.description: Pushes back on the "GDevelop is just a toy" cliché, comparing the two engines' real ceilings so indie developers can choose by project needs, not stereotypes.

item.title: Planning persistence for a small online RPG - eight data decisions to make before your first public alpha
item.description: Your save-data shape decides how easily you can patch, rebalance, roll back and recover — eight data decisions to settle before your first public alpha.

item.title: Where 3D meets the real world: highlights from Unity Industry Summit Munich 2026
item.description: From Mazda to Lufthansa, an F1 simulator and 13 demo stations, this year's Unity Industry Summit showed how AI agents, robotics and 3D data are moving into real industrial work.

item.title: GTA 6 hits $3.79 billion in its first day on sale, becoming "the biggest entertainment launch in history"
item.description: Rockstar says GTA 6 grossed $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, setting a new record for entertainment launches across any medium — a fresh benchmark for the market ceiling indie developers are working under.

item.title: GTA 6 is Officially the Biggest Entertainment Launch in History
item.description: Rockstar confirmed GTA 6 made nearly $4 billion in estimated retail sales in its first 24 hours, the biggest entertainment launch in history — a case study in turning anticipation into sales.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI is now the biggest video game launch in history
item.description: GTA VI grossed $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales and sold 32.5 million copies before release, making it the biggest game launch in history — a useful benchmark for indie developers sizing up AAA launch scale.

item.title: Fitting a 78-card game on a phone screen: lessons from a French tarot app
item.description: Building a French tarot app meant squeezing a 78-card trick-taking game onto a 6-inch landscape screen — the author shares hands-on lessons on hand layout and interface trade-offs.

item.title: Saving player data safely with DataStore in Roblox: three rules and a small manager
item.description: Lost saves are the most expensive bug a Roblox game can have, and this piece shows how three rules plus a small data manager can keep the most common save mistakes out.

item.title: A Video-First Workflow for Choosing Game Sprite Frames
item.description: Watch the motion before picking the frames: MotifDeck turns an action into continuous video, extracts and cleans up the frames, so developers can check an animation feels right before locking the sprite sheet.

item.title: A nightly-build handoff checklist for Unreal teams split between India and Europe or the US
item.description: A nightly-build handoff checklist for Unreal teams split between India and Europe or the US, agreeing on a single cutoff time and handoff routine so the time-zone gap becomes round-the-clock momentum instead of lost mornings.

item.title: Inside V.E.T.O.R — Limbo Spider Boss Fight: Canvas Architecture, Hostage Risk & Synced Video Engine
item.description: This devlog breaks down the Limbo Spider boss fight, where the boss carries a living hostage in a web cocoon and every strike must avoid the captive, built on Canvas rendering and synced video layers.

item.title: Real-Time Rendering & Simulation at Scale: Analyzing GTA 6 on the PS5 Pro
item.description: Using GTA 6 as a case study, this piece breaks down how multi-threaded physics, crowd simulation AI, and ray-traced lighting can fit inside a 16.6ms frame budget, and what trade-offs large-scale open-world rendering on console demands.

item.title: Three.js Examples: 7 Playable Games With Source Code
item.description: Seven complete Three.js games you can play in the browser right now, all with full source code open — a handy reference for learning how a 3D web game is put together.

item.title: ExLoader Not Opening? A Windows Evidence Checklist
item.description: When ExLoader won't launch, turn the failure into a checkable evidence trail with timestamped launch logs, Task Manager, and Reliability Monitor records.

item.title: Chess.com expands with 10 new classic games
item.description: Chess.com's new Classic Games platform adds 10 traditional games including Go, Shogi, and Mahjong, with AI handling the rules while humans lead the design.

item.title: CS2 Mod Config Backups: A Practical Update Checklist
item.description: Manage CS2 mod configs with versioned snapshots, one-change tests, and rollback steps, so every update is traceable and a bad patch can be undone fast.

item.title: ExLoader Download: Build a Clean Installation Record
item.description: Turn an ExLoader install into a reproducible record with release notes, SHA-256 hashes, tracked paths, and config backups, so troubleshooting follows the paper trail.
